sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Icebreaker is a location in Escape from Tarkov. It is the thirteenth map that was added to the game.

sections.heading: Description
sections.text: In the Gulf of Finland, trapped within the blockade surrounding Tarkov, lies the nuclear-powered icebreaker "Boreas", owned by the logistics corporation Paradigm Shipping. The exact purpose of "Boreas" and the cargo it carries remain unknown. It appears that Paradigm Shipping and TerraGroup made special efforts to minimize any mention of the icebreaker in the press and keep its routes and assignments classified.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This location can initially only be entered through transiting from Lighthouse or Shoreline after unlocking it in the story chapter Boreas. The transits are located at the piers and require a Sudak-Tudak marine repair kit.

- Direct access from the location selection screen is unlocked upon completing the questline Stick to It. The requirement for a Sudak-Tudak marine repair kit still applies.
- The number of encountered Black Division operatives and The Wedge's followers depends on the number of players in the raid. Detailed numbers can be found on the maps below.

sections.heading: Insurance
sections.text: All insured items left in a raid by players will not be returned. Upon death, insurance Traders will send the usual in-game mail about dispatching people to recover the items, but when the insurance timer runs out they will explain that their people don't go to the location, didn't find it or died in the process.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This location is based on the Russian "Арктика" (Arktika) nuclear-powered icebreaker.
- Initially, the icebreaker was called "Северный ветер" (North Wind) in concept art. In subsequent screenshots, the landing pad read "Сибирь" (Siberia). In the final trailer, the name was changed to "Борей" (Boreas). In ancient Greek mythology, Boreas is the personification of the stormy northern wind. Boreas was also considered the god of winter, descending from the cold mountains of Thrace, cooling the air with his icy breath.

- During the "Full Speed Ahead" event, it becomes clear that the Rogues know about the icebreaker and where to find it, specifically somewhere off the coast of the Gulf of Finland, near Tarkov. This is revealed by Rogue intel maps, which can be found on Knight.
